title: Australia: around 60% of home battery installs rated substandard
lede: Australia's Clean Energy Regulator inspected a record 6,554 home solar and battery systems in 2025–26 and found most battery faults come from installation work, not products. Here is the news in short.
bullets: Record 6,554 inspections in 2025–26 under the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme: 3,425 battery systems and 3,129 solar systems.
61.19% of batteries and 23.11% of solar systems were rated substandard (faults that must be fixed); under 1% of each were rated unsafe.
Almost all non-compliance came from poor workmanship rather than faulty equipment.
Common solar faults: wrongly sized or badly fixed cables and conduits, poor bonding/earthing of panel frames, mismatched or badly fitted DC connectors, and badly fitted mounting.
Common battery faults: missing or wrong labels, wrong or missing wiring, under-rated circuit protection and poor physical protection of cables and the battery.
Since 1 July 2025 the regulator has contacted more than 830 installers with advisory and warning letters; repeat offenders can be suspended.
thailand_note: Batteries are where installs go wrong: the fault rate was almost three times that of solar. As home batteries grow in Thailand, the same points matter: correct labels, matched DC connectors, correct breaker and fuse ratings, protected cables and torque-checked terminals. Thailand has no routine audit like this, so a maintenance visit with insulation, earthing and thermal checks is the best way to find these faults early.

title: Japan sees a 30% rise in corporate solar PPAs
lede: Japanese companies signed about 30% more corporate solar power purchase agreements in January–October 2026 than a year earlier, led by data centres but now spreading to manufacturers and railways. Here is the news in short.
bullets: Global Infrastructure Sherpa counted about 30% more corporate solar PPAs in Japan in January–October 2026 than in the same period of 2025.
Big tech keeps buying: Microsoft signed two solar PPAs with Blueleaf Energy, and a 44 MW Fukushima plant began supplying Amazon in May.
Manufacturers are joining: NSK signed a 15-year virtual PPA for 54 MW of solar plus about 130 MWh of batteries; Nippon Electric Glass signed a 20-year PPA from March 2027.
Largest deals this year: Equinix 121 MW and Tokyu Railway 98 MW.
Virtual PPAs let firms buy green certificates at a fixed price while keeping their current supplier, which brings in retailers, railways and mid-sized factories.
More than 500 corporate PPAs (over 2.5 GW) have been disclosed since 2021; Japan has about 100 GW of solar.
thailand_note: Thai businesses have similar options: on-site solar they own (the biggest bill saving), an on-site private PPA with no upfront cost, the Utility Green Tariff (UGT1/UGT2) for certificates, and a direct-PPA pilot so far limited to data centres. Start with 12 months of bills and your daytime load, use your own roof first, and read PPA terms carefully: discount versus the tariff including Ft, escalation, length and buy-out.

title: Huawei plans 5–15% price rises for solar inverters and storage
lede: Huawei Digital Power has told customers that inverter and storage prices will rise, following similar moves by other Chinese makers since August, while solar panel prices keep falling. Here is the news in short.
bullets: In a customer notice dated 20 October, Huawei proposed rises of 5–15% for residential solar-plus-storage, commercial and industrial systems and utility PV inverters.
Grid-forming utility storage, including power conversion systems, faces smaller rises of 5–10%.
No start date was given; increases will be agreed with each customer.
Reasons given: higher prices since 2025 for copper, printed circuit boards and memory chips.
Others have done the same since August, including Sungrow (5–15% from 20 September), Growatt (5–10% from 8 October) and Kehua (5–15% from 1 November).
Solar panel prices went the other way and kept falling in October.
thailand_note: For a home or business system, panels are getting cheaper while inverters, storage converters, cable and switchgear cost more, so the total may move little but the mix changes. If you hold a quotation, act within its validity and ask for fixed equipment prices; choose a hybrid inverter that can take more battery later; and never accept undersized cables or missing protection to save on copper.
